Tabulate Lineup Choices, Including Null Foils

Source: R/lineup_table.R
lineup_table.Rd

Builds a table of lineup choices with one entry for every lineup member, including members that no mock witness chose.

Usage

lineup_table(lineup_vec, k, suspect_pos = NULL)

Arguments

lineup_vec

A numeric vector of lineup choices.

k

Number of members in the lineup (suspect plus foils). Must be specified by the user (scalar).

suspect_pos

Optional position of the nominated suspect, marked in the printed output. Defaults to NULL, for lineups with no pre-specified suspect.

Value

An object of class lineup_table, inheriting from table, with k named entries. Because it inherits from table it can be passed to esize_m, esize_T and the other table-taking functions in this package unchanged.

Details

Calling table() directly on a vector of lineup choices tabulates only the positions that were actually chosen. A lineup member that no witness selected — a null foil — is silently dropped, so the resulting table has fewer than k entries and nothing in the output reveals that a member is missing. This is important because a foil nobody would pick is not a functioning alternative to the suspect, one of several things that can make a lineup unfair. A member with no choices in a small sample is not necessarily such a foil.

lineup_table() tabulates over all k positions, so unchosen members appear explicitly as zero counts, and its print method names them.

The measures in this package already handle null foils correctly when given a complete table. esize_m(), for instance, reindexes counts by position and deducts unchosen members from the adjusted estimate. What lineup_table() adds is visibility, not a change in the arithmetic.

References

Malpass, R. S. (1981). Effective size and defendant bias in eyewitness identification lineups. Law and Human Behavior, 5(4), 299-309.

Tredoux, C. G. (1998). Statistical inference on measures of lineup fairness. Law and Human Behavior, 22(2), 217-237.

See also

esize_m, esize_T, allprop

Examples

# A lineup in which position 4 was never chosen
lineup_vec <- rep(c(5, 3, 2, 1, 8, 6, 7), each = 4)

# table() drops the unchosen member: only 7 entries for an 8-person lineup
table(lineup_vec)
#> lineup_vec
#> 1 2 3 5 6 7 8 
#> 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 

# lineup_table() keeps it, and says so
lineup_table(lineup_vec, k = 8, suspect_pos = 3)
#> Lineup choices (k = 8, N = 28)
#> 
#>  pos: 1  2  3*  4  5  6  7  8
#>  cnt: 4  4   4  0  4  4  4  4
#> 
#>  * = nominated suspect
#> 
#>  Note: 1 null foil (position 4) received no choices.
#>  Unchosen members reduce effective size; see ?esize_m.

# Accepted by the effective size functions unchanged
esize_m(lineup_table(lineup_vec, k = 8), k = 8)
#> [1] 7
